utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. And good afternoon, sir. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now we commence with Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Popovski. My name is Nisha Valabhji. I am counsel for the Prosecution and I will now ask you some questions about your evidence. Now, sir you are presently the assistant minister in the sector for financial, material, technical and logistical matters within the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to speak up.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The sector which I head is the sector for material, technical, financial, and logistic matters as you mentioned. In this sector, there is voluminous work. We prepare the salaries of the employees at the MOI. We plan the budget of the Ministry of Interior. The overall procurement for the MOI, equipment, including -- from the smallest to the largest procurement issues are dealt with by our sector, registering into accounting books, preparing account balances, also securing nourishment for members of MOI when they are on the ground, also the unit for construction and maintenance of facilities which are in ownership of the MOI. We look after for the rest homes of the MOI. We secure reserve parts for vehicles, materials for printing in the Ministry of Interior warehouse facilities. This is our work. Perhaps I've omitted something, but in general, this is what we do in our sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovski. And in fact, sir, you've been employed in the Ministry of Interior since March the 15th, 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And that's when you joined the MOI as advisor in the property section at the sector in which you are currently still employed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So, in sum, Mr. Popovski, you've been working in the Ministry of Interior for close to one year. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in two weeks it will be one year.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, when were you informed by the Defence that you would have to appear personally before the ICTY. Do you recall roughly?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than ten days prior to my coming here. Perhaps a week. About ten days. In that period, I was away on business in Croatia, and when I came back exactly about a week back, then it was definitely the position that I will be coming here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: At this stage, could the court binders please be distributed?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovski, could you turn, please, to tab 1 of the binder. I think you're already there. If you just flip that over, you'll see something that may be familiar to you. This is the statement which you provided to the Defence on the 28th of September, 2007. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And could you turn now, sir, to tab 2 of the binder. And please have a look at the first couple of pages there, Mr. Popovski. Now, there is your Rule 92 bis statement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: On January 22nd, 2008, you met with the registry officer and you were given a further opportunity to review your statement.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Could we have a look at paragraph 3 of your statement, sir. And in paragraph 3, you say that from the Defence you were given a list of 40 persons. Do you see that in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4, sir, of your statement, you say that you are signing and submitting the list as appendix to this statement. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you gave the attestation for your statement, that is when you met with the registry court officer, at that time in January of this year it was made clear to you, wasn't it, that your statement would be given in evidence in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could you look, then, at the page which bears the number on the lower right-hand corner, 1D00-9992, and I believe it's the third page in the pagination. Are you there, sir, at 1D00-9992, we're still in tab 2 of the binder. Okay. Now, in the middle of the page there are the words: Additional remarks. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if this is what have you in mind, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. And it sets out what this package consists of. And then it states: "The following document was before the witness at the time of certification. A list of 40 names signed by the witness, single-page document." Do you see that, sir, on this page?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, it's true, isn't it that at the time of this attestation procedure you declined to include this 40-person list in this Rule 92 bis package. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, when you met with the registry court officer and you were given a chance to go over your statement and to confirm it, you declined to include, at that time, the list of 40 persons that's referred to in paragraph 3 of your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I met with the representative from the Tribunal, I signed the statement. This was the attestation of the statement which I had previously signed and the list of 40 persons. Nothing more than that came into question. I just signed or confirmed the previously given statement with the list of 40 persons, where I mentioned that only eight of those persons were engaged as part of the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I see that my colleague is on her feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to clarify, the witness responded to the question, but the suggestion of the court officer was that he should not add the appendices to the statement, because this was just a verification of the statement and this is in accordance your position to the 92 bis rule, when it was necessary for accepting the statement for the witness to be called. The witness already mentioned he was only in effect verifying his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 5 of your Rule 92 bis statement, you say that you made insight into the Ministry of Interior's archive and its sector for finances. Now, this was the first review that you performed in relation to these 40 persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly - perhaps this is a game of words. Firstly, this was given to the services from my sector to check with the services at SVR Skopje. Once I was told when meeting with the representative of the Tribunal there was no mention of whether I should be coming to The Hague or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, I'm afraid, because I am not sure that you understood the gist of my question. Perhaps I wasn't very clear. In paragraph 5 of your statement, you refer to having made an insight into the ministry's archive and in the sector for finances and you speak of a check that was conducted. And I simply want to know, is that the first round of checks that you carried out last year in 2007, July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right. The sector of finance conducted a check and since none of the listed persons is not on the payroll whereby the payroll of all employees at the MOI is led by my sector, since none of these persons were on the payroll, it means that none of them were employed at the MOI, nor did they drew their salaries from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, you say that the sector of finance conducted a check. I'd just like to inquire a little further from you, did you personally carry out any checks during this first round, in 2007?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my sector, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And what exactly did you do at that time?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the check was made in my sector, and once we concluded that none of these persons is in regular employment at the MOI, this list, the services from my sector were in contact with the sectors of SVR Skopje which have the lists and the calculations for remuneration of the reserve structures. Then these services checked which of these 40 persons were engaged within the reserve structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. But I just want to be clear, sir. At that time, did you yourself undertake any of these checking activities personally, or were these officials in your sector in contact with the SVR Skopje?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in my sector I did this together with my services. Later on, there was done at SVR Skopje and their relevant services. I personally joined this at a somewhat later date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Well, with regard to the checks that were done in 2007, how are the records kept, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Records are kept by SVR Skopje. Each of the documents which I checked for the persons regardless of the time-period when they may be engaged even if for one day, such person must be remunerated. There are such lists for remuneration kept by SVR Skopje. At that period of time, these lists were kept by SVR Skopje, and then our sector is informed to transfer a certain amount at a given and designated bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the persons from your sector that carried out this check, did you supervise their work in any way?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in our cooperation with the services from SVR Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's right. When persons from your sector were undertaking these checks, did they call you with queries, did you have the occasion to supervise them in what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible always to do this. I mentioned previously all of the obligations we are charged with. Therefore, we cannot always fully focus on one issue. I have trust in my services. I cannot exactly say how long it took them to check what they were supposed to do, but ultimately I received information from them that these eight persons were engaged from the 1st of August to the 30th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Right. And this was the information which, in fact, you then adopted in your statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And just to summarize briefly, sir, in paragraph 6 of your statement, this information states that: "Eight persons were engaged in the Ministry of Interior as police reservists and received salaries for the period 1st of August, 2001, to 20th September, 2001," is that correct, as it says in paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, just prior to coming here to give your testimony, you decided to check personally certain lists kept in the SVR Skopje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And just to be really clear on this, you checked the lists pertaining to salaries received. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said salary is one thing, remuneration another. The check of the salaries is done in our sector, because we prepare the payroll. In the second case, this is not a salary, rather, remuneration for persons engaged in the reserve forces which are kept in this case by SVR Skopje; and because I was told that I was due to come here, I wanted, once again, personally, with the services, to check the truthfulness and one mistake was noted of which I made mention during my previous statements. Sometimes it is a matter of omission, and in other cases this was a matter of misspelling, typing errors, change of name, Boris, Boris or Boro, whether the last naming ended in -ov or -ovski and mistakes of this kind. Again, this was the last week prior to my arrival here. If you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Well, sir, as a matter of fact, you found a number of mistakes in the original findings. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said this, that six additional people were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So, as a result, instead of eight persons having been found to have received compensations, salaries, however one wants to word it, for their engagement in the Ministry of Interior reserve police, 14 persons were found to have received salaries in total. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And 14 persons, that's more than a third of the list of the 40 persons that you were asked to check. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I did not calculate the percentages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, in relation to these six additional persons whom you found to have received salaries, compensation, you testified last week that as to two persons Sladimovski Zoran and Cankulovski Borce, that this represented a classic omission. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said last week, in giving my testimony, that there were 14 names in question; I don't know them and I could not know them all by heart. I mentioned these two as persons where omissions have been made. I did not say that this was the definitive number. I mentioned them as persons where such omissions were made. And I also said that they're other omissions, again not to repeat myself again, mistakes in typing, mistakes in spelling, a letter or two in one's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you made this most recent check because you were concerned about the accuracy of the prior review. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps one could not say this, that I was concerned. I told you previously, I have full trust in the work by my services. But I wanted to again look and go through these lists personally and to make sure that everything was all right. Because it is -- it is not always possible to do this for myself, to become personally engaged there matters. If this were so, 24 hours would not be sufficient for a supervisor to do this. This is why work is given to the services and this is why I say I have full trust in the work they do. We have full cooperation between us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: But as a matter of fact, you did decide to become quite personally engaged this time around, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said so. I did want to check this personally and to make sure it was all right. There's an old proverb that says more eyes see better than one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned that you can't recall all the names that have now been added to the list of persons that you found to receive salaries. Now, in the proofing note which we were provided by my colleagues across the way, following their meeting with you last week, we were provided with a list of six persons, of six additional persons, and one of them is Zoran Sladimovski, and the other one is an Ilija Sekerovski.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember these two names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And in fact, if you look at the list of 40 persons, which is at tab 1 of the binder, you see these two people on the list, don't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Number 9 is Sladimovski Zoran; and 18 Sekerovski Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. So, sir, you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that these two persons were not found in the original review that was done in July 2007 of the register of reservists in the SVR Skopje. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they are not written among these eight, then it means that they were not seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: What this means, sir, isn't it that the list of reservists in the SVR Skopje doesn't fully represent all persons who were reservists at the time?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, you are now asking me about something which you said yourself I have been in the Ministry of Interior affairs for a year. I never worked in the MOI before. So now you are asking me about something that would require for me to speculate. I think I told you very well; sometimes it is just a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you. You haven't answered my question. So I will repeat it. And the question was: These two names were not found in the original review that was done in July 2007 and that means, doesn't it, sir, that the list of reservists in the SVR Skopje doesn't fully reflect all the persons who were reservists at that time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand why you don't want to understand me. Our sector and me in the capacity of the head of the sector have no contact points with the reserve police. The most meritable lists are those where you can see that the person should be compensated for their work which means that this person has been engaged. I reiterate this is obviously a flaw. I don't know whether to say there are more than one list. I don't know why you don't understand me. Those lists are kept in the SVR Skopje and my sector does not have any connection with SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's not what asked you. And again, I don't think you have answered my question. Now, you have said that the most meritable lists are those regarding compensation. And in fact in your testimony last week, you said: "Lists with compensation I checked in SVR Skopje because persons from the list are on the SVR Skopje lists. They have a list of reservists, however, the list which is reliable is that for the compensation." Do you recall this testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But that list as well is found in the SVR Skopje. So the remuneration list is in the SVR Skopje, while our sector receives an information from SVR Skopje how much money should be transferred in a designated bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: By implication, sir, what you're really saying that the list pertaining to compensations is more reliable than a list that purports to be a list of reservists. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the proofing note which we were provided last week, there were four other names that were given to us regarding persons who received compensation. And these persons were written as Borce Cankulovski, Dragi Mackimov, Zoran Kostencovski, and Ljubomir Milosevski. Could you look again at the list of persons in tab 1, please.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And you see there --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- think of that list --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: You see that there item number 10, person number 10, rather, is Cankulovski Bojko Borce and this corresponds to Borce Cankulovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cankulovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Cankulovski. Thank you for correcting me. And person number 30 is a Mackinovski Dime Dragi. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And that is the person referred to, isn't it, as Dragi Mackimov in the proofing note. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's Mackinov. I wouldn't be 100 per cent sure. I think it's a mistake. It should be Mackinov.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: What should be Mackinov? In this list of 40 persons.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said so these additional six persons where a mistake was noticed, typing errors mainly. Here it is Mackinovski and that is why I'm saying I'm not 100 per cent sure whether this person was Mackinov without -ski or Mackinovski, something like that. Whether the mistake is in the third letter, whether it should be Ch instead of C or the -ski should be omitted, I'm not sure. I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So in short you're not entirely sure about all of the information that you were asked to check. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty now whether this person is with ski or his last name should contain the letter Ch, I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Person at number 32 of this list is Kostencovski Bozin, Zoran and that's the person referred to as Zoran Kostencovski in the proofing note. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is Kostensov Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now the fourth person mentioned in the proofing note is Ljubomir Milosevski. Could you look again at this list of 40 persons, sir, there is no Ljubomir Milosevski in the list, is there, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is Milosevski Sande, Ljuboten, here. There is a mistake in his name, as far as I can see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And indeed it should say Sande instead of Sandre. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the father's name. It is possible that it is Aleksander or Sande Milosevski, Sande Ljubomir. I think it's Sande. I think it's Sande.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Sir, could you turn now to tab 21 of the binder?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, last week you provided some documents to the Defence when you came to The Hague. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And in fact, this is part of the set of documents that you brought with you to The Hague. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And this set of documents sets out lists of police reservists at PS Cair in the period between the 16th and 31st of August, 2001, who received salaries or remuneration. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And could you turn, then, to the page N006-9742.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And about halfway down the page, next to the number 16019, do you see the name Sande Milosevski, sir? That's what that says, doesn't it. Just yes or no, sir, would do.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, you said N006-9742.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the person Milosevski Ljubomir..

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at the middle --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16, you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: 16019 in the middle of the page. It's quite squarely in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So you would agree that name says Sande Milosevski. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you could turn to the page N006-9753. Close to the bottom of the page, sir, in handwriting text, do you see, again the name Sande Milosevski. That's what that says, sir, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will become Exhibit P586.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, line 15, the colleague said this was lists from PS Cair and this is from the PS Kuceviste. Since now they have been accepted as exhibits, this should be correct what we are actually accepting. These are lists from PS Kuceviste. Of course they are within Cair, but it is a completely separate police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I would only note, Your Honours, that on the first page, at N006-9739 the document refers to PS Cair, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The reference to OVR Cair, you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Actually, there are two references, one is the upper left-hand side and that is OVR Cair, RPS Kuceviste. But in the text of the communication it refers to PS Cair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I don't know if anything is going to turn on this, but we are, unless counsel are agreed, in a position only to rely on what is actually given in evidence. So if there is any issue that you think is important, Ms. Residovic, you may have to try and deal with it in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, could you now turn to tab 20 of the binder. Have you found it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. And please look at the page N006-9757. This is a similar list, isn't it, sir, for the period the 1st of September, 2001, until the 30th of September, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And, again, this is part of the documentation which you provided to the Defence last week upon coming to The Hague. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you turn to page -- actually, if you turn the page, to N006-9758.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's the name Sande Milosevski again, the fourth name from the bottom of the page. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: If you turn to the page N006-9762, sir.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: In the middle of the page there's the name again, Sande Milosevski. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could this be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P587, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovski, you were asked very recently to review a list of eight names previously given to Mr. Spase Filipov to review. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And you were not asked at any prior time to review this additional list of names. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you could turn to tab 9 of the binder. This is the list of names, sir, isn't it, that Mr. Filipov was originally asked to review?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And you reviewed this list and determined that nobody from this list received any remuneration. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And two of the persons on this list are a Blagoja Mladenovski and Mile Milevski. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could we turn now to tab 18 of the binder. And, again --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: -- this is part of the documents which you brought with you last week. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, if you allow me a second or two. For OVR Cair, yes, I think those are the documents that I brought.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Indeed. And it sets out police reservists at PS Cair who received salaries in the period between the 1st of August, 2001, and the 30th of -- or, rather, the 31st of August, 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could we then turn to page N006-9774 in this document.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And about a third of the way down the page, sir, that's the name Blagojce Mladenovski. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And Blagojce is a nickname for Blagoje, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm that. Blagojce exists as a name just like Blagoje. In the Republic of Macedonia there is a name Blagojce and there is also a name Blagoje. I couldn't confirm whether this is a nickname for Blagoje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Isn't it possible, sir, that Blagojce is indeed a nickname for Blagoje, isn't it possible?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't say. I couldn't confirm, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P588, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And could we turn, sir, to tab 19 of the binder. Again, sir, you're familiar with this question, of course. This is part of the documents that you brought with you last week, and they show reservists at PS Cair who received salaries in September 2001. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And could you turn to page N006-9722.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And the penultimate name at the bottom of the page, sir, that's Mile Milevski, isn't it? That's what that says, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as you can see, for the request for the data under item 8, the Defence requested data for Milevski Dejan. And I don't know, as we can see from our request under item 8, we requested data for Milevski Dejan, and I don't see the relevance of the document that my learned colleague is proposing, because this document does not refer to Milevski Dejan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the document, as the witness has pointed out, refers to a Mile Milevski and the request in question, which is now Exhibit 1D263 that Mr. Filipov was supposed to work on, refers to a Mile Dejan Milevski. That is item 8 of 1D263. And may I add, Your Honour, that I do not see an issue at this stage of admissibility of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it would be correct if the witness sees this document and if he could explain what the middle name means, and that might give the Chamber a better view what Defence actually wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask that the microphones that are not in use be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The exhibit will be received, Ms. Residovic. If you want to re-examine on the matter, you may do so, or else it may be a matter of contentious fact that has to be the subject of submission and decision.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become the Exhibit P589, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovski, you weren't working in the Ministry of Interior in 2001, were you?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So in 2001, therefore, you were not able to observe how records were made and kept in the Ministry of Interior. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's logical. If I wasn't working in 2001, then I couldn't have insight in many issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Very well. And because you couldn't have insight in many issues, in fact, you have no direct knowledge concerning the creation and maintenance of these lists which you brought with you to The Hague last week. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, sir, you can't yourself be entirely sure that these additional lists are also complete. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any other lists except this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: But that wasn't the question, sir, that I asked you. My question was: You can't be entirely sure because you were not involved with the creation and maintenance of these lists generated in 2001, that these are complete lists. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Since I was not employed then, that means that I was not involved with this issue of the lists. But I say once again, I did not see any other lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, it's true, isn't it, that 2001 was a very difficult year, a difficult period of time in Macedonia. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the context of the question. In 2001, I was employed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Sir, I --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia. Therefore, I do not understand the question -- the context in which you asked this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Fair enough. Well, I'll explain to you the context. We've heard evidence in this case, sir, that the security situation in Macedonia in 2001 was very complex and that the Ministry of Interior was extremely pressed with work at this point in time. We've also heard evidence from a Defence witness to the effect that in such a situation as the one the prevailed in 2001, things had to be done, perhaps, more quickly and flexibly. And with that, sir, I would ask you when persons are working in conditions of stress, you'd agree that they might carry out their duties in a way that would differ from how they would carry them out in peacetime. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've listed a number of thesis from my colleagues who were here who were employed at that time. If they say that this is so, then this is so. Now you're asking me to say something which could be but speculation on my part. We don't know. Some persons do better under conditions of deadlines, or, as you say, under conditions of stress. We could not say this. And I also wouldn't be able to tell you this, how people react or act under a given situation. Each people reacts -- all people react different --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. But you would agree, sir, wouldn't you, that it's possible that in such times record keeping may not have been as meticulously done as would be the case in peacetime. Would you agree that that is a possibility?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have to say yet once again. I cannot speculate about things which happened almost six years prior to my employment at the MOI. I really am not able to speculate on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovski, looking again at your statement in tab 2, paragraph 6 of your statement you set out the names of eight individuals whom -- who were found to be members of the reserve police and received salaries at that point in time. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they received remuneration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And three of the persons whom you have listed in paragraph 6 are Tome Sarkoski, Stojan Kostencovski and Ljupco Stojanovski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could you now turn to the document at tab 5 of your binder. This is N000-5187.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated the 13th of November, 2003. It's from the section for Defence preparations of the Ministry of Interior, and it's to the SVR Skopje. And its subject is review of the records concerning persons from OVR Cair engaged as volunteers in the reserve composition of the police. Do you see that, in the subject header?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. And further down it says: "In connection to the list of persons from OVR Cair, who were voluntarily engaged in OVR Cair," and there's a serial number and a date. "Prepared by OOP," and that, I believe, refers to the sector for Defence preparation, "with SVR Skopje and the actual request to make a list of persons who have received uniforms and weapons although they had already been tried for different criminal acts and after the review of the records, we inform you of the following" and then there appears a list of names. Are you with me so far, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, we see a list of names, and the first name is Ljupco Stojanovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And it says that in 1996 he was sentenced to three months imprisonment but the sentence was suspended for a year. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And, for the record, I refer to P00081, which sets out Article 155 of the Macedonian Criminal Code in 1996. Well, sir, isn't this the same name that appears in paragraph 6 of your statement that we just looked at in the list of persons whom we found received compensation?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if we look at the second page of this document in tab 5, and that is N000-5187, now the third name listed on the Macedonian version of this page is Tome Sarkoski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And it says that in 1998, he was given a fine for committing a crime under Article 44 of the KZM. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, going back to the list of eight persons in your statement, sir, that's one of the persons that you found to be a reserve police officer within the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And could we turn briefly to tab 13 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And here we see the cover page of a publication and it is entitled criminal law of the socialist Republic of Macedonia, third amended publication, 1998. Do you see that sir? It's a little hard to read perhaps.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you turn the page, sir, you see that Article 44 refers to light bodily injury. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could we turn to the document under tab 5, once again. And if you look, sir, further down on page N000-5188.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: You see the name Kostencovski Stojan. Do you see that name, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And next to the name it says that in 1963, he was sentenced to two months of imprisonment suspended for a year for committing a crime under Article 259 of the Criminal Code of Yugoslavia. And in 1968, he was sentenced to a year and six months of strict imprisonment for committing a crime under Article 141 of the KZJ. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, that is another individual whom you found to be a police reservist in August/September 2001, and who was mentioned in your statement at paragraph 6. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kostencovski Stojan.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: All right. Could we turn briefly then to tab 14 of the binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And do you see there the cover page of a publication. And it is from 1968, and the cover page says that it's the Criminal Code of the SFRY, copyright 1968, Belgrade. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you turn, sir, to Article 141, paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And it says there: "The one who will cause serious bodily injury to another person or will cause serious disturbance to another's health will be penalised by imprisonment of at least six months or severe imprisonment of up to a five-year period." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I forget, could this please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean tab 5?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I mean at present tab 14 and tab 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, tab 14 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P590, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tab 13 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P591, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, Mr. Popovski, in addition to the eight persons listed in your statement as having received salaries, you've just told us that your more recent check revealed that Ilija Sekerovski also received remuneration. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And there we must go back to tab 5. Looking at page N000-5187. Pardon me, 5188 at the top of the page in Macedonian. Do you see there the name Ilija Sekerovski, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And do you see written next to that name it says in 1974, he was given a fine of 1000 dinars for crime against public security of the KZM and other crimes. In 1994, he was sentenced to one year of imprisonment, suspended to three years under Article 178. In 1985, he was sentenced to six months of imprisonment under Article 239 and 243 of the KZM. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P592, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you could turn to tab 17 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And do you see there the criminal law of the Socialist Republic of Macedonia and it says on the first page at the bottom that this law is amended with the law of amendment of the criminal law of the Socialist Republic of Macedonia, Official Gazette of SRM number 23/84. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you could turn the page to Article 239 of this code. Do you see that it refers to jeopardising safety and traffic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you turn to page 272 of this criminal law and Article 243 which appears on the left-hand side of the Macedonian version. Do you see that Article 243 refers to severe acts against the safety of the persons and property in traffic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be -- please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's suggested this may already be Exhibit P81.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I don't believe this to be the case, Your Honour. I believe that P81 refers to the Criminal Code enacted in July of 1996, whereas these particular provisions that we have just looked at are from a different publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have a 65 ter number then?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: The 65 ter number is 1224.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see the time. It occurs to me that if we had a break now, our normal first break, that you might discuss with the registry officer and resolve which document is which, and we can deal with that when we resume after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: We shall certainly do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now and resume at 20 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the delay. We hope that the technical issues are now overcome. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just before the break, Your Honour, I had sought to tender a 65 ter 1224 and having conferred with the registry officer during the break, we have established that P00081 is indeed a distinct exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You now tender and it will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could 65 ter 1224 please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit P592, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that is the document, for our purposes, at tab --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: It's at tab 17, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 17. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Correction, Your Honours, this will become Exhibit P593.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Popovski, if you could turn to tab 6 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the special police unit the Lions?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had been in the Ministry of Interior Affairs for just 11 months. So I don't know what your question refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I merely wanted to ascertain, sir, whether you had some familiarity with this police unit. But we can move on --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: This unit operated sometime in 2001 and if we look at this document at N006 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know that cross-examination does not have to stick to the statement of the witness, but I cannot see the relevance of it because there is nothing about Lions in the statement, and the witness said that he didn't know anything about that because he had sent only 10 months in the ministry. So I would like to know why these questions are being asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, hopefully it will become clear in a moment whether it is something that the witness can deal with or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you could turn to page N006-7243, you're probably there already I see. This is Article dated the 9th of November, 2002, and it's entitled the MVR spent one-fifth of next year's budget and the article contains remarks made by Minister Hari Kostov at a press conference. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And if you look at the last few paragraphs and this is on page 2 of the English version, it states: "Lions will be transformed, confirmed the new minister but did he not say explicitly when and how it will happen. He reiterated that more than a thousand members of the Lions did not possess decisions on employment and all of them who are found to be professionals, competent and without a criminal record will be appointed to appropriate structures in the Ministry of Interior." Sir, you would agree with me that according to what this article states, over a thousand Lions members did not have decisions on employment. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speculate about something that happened on the -- in 2002 and it was said by Mr. Hari Kostov. So you are asking me to say something or to comment on something that was said five years ago by another person, whether this was a comment or an attitude or a stance I really don't know whether I should agree or disagree with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: But you would agree, sir, that according to the text that I've just read out that is what it says there. Isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, since it is written, but whether the written is true and what Mr. Hari Kostov meant by it, I really cannot say. But undoubtedly I can read just as you and it is obvious that Mr. Kostov has said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph we see that it says: "Kostov, however, did not say how many of the Lions have criminal records, but he emphasised that those who had would not be engaged any further." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour I would seek to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis is it shown to be admissible?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: It is the -- it would simply be, Your Honour, that the witness has gone through these paragraphs and is able to say that this is what he saw in the article presented to him. That is the basis, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir, that there were many mistakes in the check of Ministry of Interior records which you and others on your behalf conducted in July 2007. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. Several mistakes had happened, but it is a relative thing whether you consider them too many or too few.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And I further put it to you that the register of reservists in the SVR Skopje is not reliable and is incomplete. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning I said that my field of work and the field of work of my sector does not include this list, and I really wouldn't like to speculate or to expose certain stances of mine, not knowing whether this is true or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I put it to you that several of the individuals whom you ultimately found to have received salaries or compensation in August and September 2001 had criminal records.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And, finally, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, could all the microphones that are not in use please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, I put it to you that the lists which you provided to the Defence last week may not fully contain all compensated police reservists in August and September 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original list was amended with additional six names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: You may have misunderstood my last question, sir. I was referring to the documents which you brought with you last week to The Hague upon arriving in The Hague. And it is these documents that I am now asking you about and I put it to you that these lists may not fully contain all compensated police reservists in the period August and September 2001. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you are putting me to say the same answer. That is not within my field of work or the sector's field of work. So I wouldn't like to speculate on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any re-examination, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I do have a couple of questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovski, you remember that my learned colleague showed you your statement, the statement that was certified by an official of this Tribunal, in particular paragraph 5, and I would like to you look at this document after paragraph 2. That's 1D326.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After tab 2. No, no, I do apologise. Paragraph 3. So could you please look at the document after tab 2. Yes, I misspoke. So this is your statement. Paragraph 5 in your statement. That's Exhibit 1D326. You remember that my learned colleague showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And regarding paragraph 5 you said that you had personally checked all the lists, the salary lists kept in your sector. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to ascertain whether any persons out of the 40 persons that you checked had in fact received salaries in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salaries, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the 40 persons, were they actually employed by the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You went through paragraph 6 with my learned colleague, the checks for the compensations for the reservists that were kept and are kept today in the sector in Skopje. Do you recall having discussed that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to wait until the question of Ms. Residovic is translated before he replies. Thank you very much. Could the witness now repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question now. Do you recall that you discussed with my learned colleague the paragraph 6 in your statement about the checks that were done on the reservists that were engaged in the sector of the interior in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where are the lists of all the reservists that are engaged kept, the lists of their engagement and the -- any payments of any remunerations?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, in SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you decided to go through those lists together with the services, were you able to check all the lists for all the persons that had received compensation in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make copies of all those lists and did you hand them to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like you to look at the document at tab 21. That's P586. Do you remember discussing this with my learned colleague? Actually, you talked about some persons that had received some form of compensation in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please go to tab 21, to page N006-9739, that's the Macedonian version. The English version would be N006-9739. Do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who submitted this document?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is said here the Ministry of Interior Affairs of Macedonia, sector of interior affairs Skopje, OVR Cair, subject completed review, submits. So it means that it was submitted to the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is RPS Kuceviste among the addressees -- or, rather, the party that sent the document?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, RPS Kuceviste as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of RPS Kuceviste, Taskovski Marjanco [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the body of this document, towards the end it is stated that this is an overview of the VPO from the PS Cair who were engaged in the period between the 16th of August, 2001 and the 31st of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what do those dates mean?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously they state the period and the list of people that were engaged within that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at page N006-9742, that was also shown to you by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether here, after item number 16 it is again written RPS Kuceviste?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please move it further up on the screen so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After item number 16, we again see RPS Kuceviste. Mr. Popovski, what police station do all those lists pertain to, the list that you've just seen?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kuceviste.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask you to look at document at tab 9. It was also shown to you by my learned colleague. And that's 1D263.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were shown the name of the person listed under number 8. Do you remember that? Exhibit 1D263.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what does the first name Milevski refer to? What is it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milevski is a last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this name in the middle, between the two names at the two ends, what is it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the father's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the last name?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the personal name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, could you please tell me, is the usual way in which names are listed in Macedonia precisely as we can see it here, first we have the last name, and then the father's name is in the middle, and then the first name?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please read the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milevski Mile Dejan.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And without the father's name?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milevski Dejan.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at the document at tab 19.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the witness and counsel are kindly asked to make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P589.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2. That's N006-9722.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't have the page, the relevant page on the screen. P589, the page is N006-9722. In the English version, under 07128, we have the name Mile Milevski. Could you please tell me, Mr. Popovski, does this name have anything to do with the name Dejan Milevski?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask you to go to tab 5 and to look at P592. You may recall that my learned colleague from the Prosecution showed you this document and asked you a number of questions pertaining to this document.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to make any checks regarding this person or any other persons regarding their criminal records?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever run any checks and do you know whether the information contained in here is correct?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, since you worked in the Ministry of Interior for almost a year, and after graduating from the law school, did you ever do anything related to criminal law or criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have any experience in keeping records, criminal records of various -- of any people?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me whether you have ever encountered in practice a situation where judgments or judicial decisions or rulings would be expunged, any such decisions against any persons?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a lawyer, do you know that after a certain period of time any penalties imposed or sanctions imposed are expunged from the records?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be positive about my answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since some sections of the SFRY Criminal Code have been tendered into evidence in relation to some questions that have been asked, I would like the witness to be shown a document that we have obtained from the Tribunal's library, if we could show to the witness this document, and that would complete my re-direct examination of this witness. Could we please have the first page of this document up on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I interrupt, please, Ms. Residovic. Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I wonder if I might be provided a copy. I don't believe I have a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honours, we obtained this document from the library during the break, and after asking questions we will make copies available to our colleagues and to the Trial Chamber, because we have this only in Serbo-Croatian, and I would have to read the relevant Article that I want to draw Your Honours' attention to in light of the evidence that has already been admitted and tendered actually by the Prosecution regarding the judgments against persons that has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you may have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Popovski, it says here that this is an overview of the Criminal Code of the SFRY that was put together by Professor Vlado Kambovski [phoen]. And Professor Kambovski is a professor in Macedonia, is he not? And this document, as can you see, is the Criminal Code of the SFRY. It's written in those big block letters.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That would be the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, right?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to go to Article 93. That's at page 49. This is a provision of the Criminal Code of the SFRY pertaining to the expunging of the -- any judgments entered against somebody.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is something that you know, as a lawyer you know that convictions, the expunging of convictions is something that can be found in the general part of the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to us read this provision. Paragraph 1 reads as follows: "A decision on the judicial caution or admonition and the decision whereby the perpetrator of a crime, a decision was made not to impose any sanction or punishment, shall be expunged from the criminal record if the convicted person does not commit a new crime within the period of one year from the day when the decision of the court becomes final." Paragraph 2: "A suspended sentence shall be expunged from the criminal record after one year from the date when the period of suspension expired, if, within that time-period, the convicted person has not committed a new crime." Paragraph 3: "A decision to impose a fine shall be expunged from the criminal record upon the expiry of three years from the date when the sentence was enforced, when the statute of limitations expired, or when a pardon was declared, if within that time-period a convicted person has not committed a new crime." Paragraph 4: "Sentences up to one year in prison and sentences of juvenile prison shall be expunged from the criminal record, upon the expiry of five years from the date when the said sentence was served, when the statute of limitations expired, or, when pardon was granted, if within that time-period the convict has not committed a new crime." Paragraph 5: "The court may, upon the petition of the convict, decide that a prison sentence longer than one year but up to a maximum of three years may be expunged from the criminal record if five years have expired from the date when the sentence was served, when the statute of limitations expired, or, when the pardon was granted, if in that time-period, the convict has not committed a new crime." You can see that that's what it says in the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, once the judgments are expunged pursuant to the Criminal Code and the time limitations stipulated therein from the criminal records, persons who check whether somebody has a criminal record or not, can they find any information about any previous convictions, if such convictions have been expunged?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this excerpt from the Criminal Code of the SFRY into evidence. We will upload it. We will have it translated and it is an integral part of the articles of the law that my learned colleague from the Prosecution has already tendered into evidence and has indeed been admitted by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would be -- I'm sorry, it would be appropriate first to receive the translation so that there is an opportunity for it to be considered by the Prosecution, and if there is no objection, it can then be received into evidence. But, at the moment, I think as it is untranslated it would be premature to receive it at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would it be possible to get a MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be and it will be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would become 1D329, Exhibit marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is MFI P594; is that correct? I beg your pardon, it's 1D. Yes. What was the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D329, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to hear, sir, that that concludes the questions for you. We would thank you for your attendance in The Hague. You are now able to return to your ordinary affairs and the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
