utterances.text: I believe Mr. Mettraux has some questions for you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon sir. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with my colleague Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like first to ask you to name or to state your name for the record as well as the date and place of your birth.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: My name is Dimitrov Branislav. I was born on the 5th of July, 1961 in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate very briefly what educational background you have in and in particular whether you hold any degrees from a university?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: I have graduated from the faculty of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you state in what place or what university?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: I graduated at the university in Skopje, the University Cyril and Methodius, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that presently you are the director of the bed and breakfast and restaurant known as Dal Met Fu. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: It is correct that since 1993 till today I am a director and one of the owners of the hotel and restaurant as you said, Dal Met Fu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was the grand extent of the introductory questions, Your Honour. We have binders for Your Honour at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, they were unnecessary and you know better, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, while the binders are being distributed and will you receive a copy of one of those, were you at some stage called by a representative of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski who wished to meet with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux. I don't know what you're proposing to do. We have got a 92 bis statement. That you tendered. That has been received. Now you cannot now treat this witness as a full witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We understand, Your Honour the only reason why this is done is not in relation to the statement, Your Honour, but in relation to the documents which have been MFI'd in relation to which we will ask a few questions. Those I wish to explore very briefly, Your Honour. The circumstances under which those copies were being made so that when asking about this document, I will be in a position to do so. It does not relate, apart from one question, to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're saying the documents that you're going to put to the witness were provided to you by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That answer you can get from him with one question and proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, is it correct that at some stage on the day when you were asked by the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski to provide a statement you also provided copies of the records of the guest books of your hotel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence lawyer Godzo called me, approached me and asked me to do this, which in turn I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the checks you carried out in those records and the documents that you gave to Mr. Godzo were carried out or were done on the day when you gave the statement to the member of the Defence team. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. On the same day when we saw each other, I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could I ask to you turn, please, to tab number 1 of your binder. For the record, this would be Rule 65 ter 1D1251. And perhaps I will ask you -- it would be under tab 1, Mr. Dimitrov. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your binder, I'd like to ask to you turn to the last page in tab 1. That would be a statement in the Macedonian language. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I see the statement in the Macedonian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recognise that statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. This is the statement which I gave to Mr. Dragan Godzo as I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the Macedonian version, could you tell whose signature is at the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: It is my signature at the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that statement true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: This statement is as true and as accurate as I believe it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just one matter of clarification, if I may. At paragraph 2 of this paragraph [sic], you indicated that the register of guests must be kept for seven years. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. When the representatives of the Tribunal came for the verification of this statement, I was told that this -- the records were kept for seven years, which I had already made mention to her when I checked with my accountants.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the sake of clarification, could you indicate who gave you this information, that such records should or had to be kept for seven years?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: I said I'm not sure whether I read it somewhere or perhaps this was something which my accountant told me, whether I heard this from my accountant.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I would seek to tender this document pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1D330.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just a moment ago, Mr. Dimitrov, I asked you a number of questions about records that you were asked to look into by members of -- or a member of the Defence team of Mr. Boskoski, and after you made those verifications of your records, did you provide copies of certain parts of the records which you had reviewed?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I allowed and I gave to one of the Defence team to obtain these documents. They were submitted to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will come back in a moment, Mr. Dimitrov, to the actual content of the books in question. But at this stage, I will ask the registry to show what is Rule 65 ter 1077. And, Mr. Dimitrov, this would be tab 5 of your binder. I'm sorry if I misspoke. This would be Rule 65 ter 1077, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist, the tab number 5 that we have is actually Exhibit P542. It's actually the first page of --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is actually a slightly different set of pictures, Your Honour. This is larger in scope than the previous one. But I'm grateful to my colleague for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, do you recognise the picture or do you recognise the document that is on the picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this. This is a guest book from the bed and breakfast Dal Met Fu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record we have in our possession at this stage the original of the two books and if there is any need, we could present the original to the witness or to the Court, if there is any wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, before we go into the contents of that document. And I'll ask the registry now, please, to turn to page N003-8114, please. Mr. Dimitrov, could you indicate what we now see on the screen? What is it?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: What we're looking at now, those are the last pages of the two books which Mr. Godzo was interested in. In effect, what we're seeing now are seals from the Macedonian police about the accuracy and reliability of these books.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you perhaps explain for the Chamber how the reliability and accuracy of the record are ensured. Perhaps could you describe how this seal comes to be put into your book.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: First of all, we buy these books from bookstores. Then we prepare the holes in the book. We have -- we thread these books, and then as such we take them to the police where they're checked and are sealed and whereby what is written here is stated, which means that nothing from then on can be changed in those books.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And simply as an indication, if you can focus on the top book on that picture, do you see a slight crack on the stamp of that top book? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how that slight crack of the stamp of the police came to occur?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: This slight crack, unfortunately, happened when Mr. Thomas, and I apologise I don't know his last name, when Mr. Thomas wanted to look into the books, I presume wanting to see whether everything is in good order with them, even without wanting to do so, I don't know, perhaps this is something that he did unwittingly. This is what the receptionist told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record this issue which is quite important was not put to Mr. Thomas Kuehnel when he was cross-examined by my learned colleague, and I believe that that issue should have been put at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague is quite right. We only learned about the crack over the weekend when the witness brought us the book in question. We had no idea up to that point what was the reason or the cause of the crack in question. If we can move now to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In a moment, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, continue, please, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If the registry could please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, could you say what we -- or could you describe what we see now on this picture?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: This picture shows the first page of both books. In the left corner, there is the thread binding the book, and then the right angle is the stamp of Dal Met Fu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does the little cord that we see in the middle of the page go through the entire book?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. They go through the whole book, and on the previous picture, you could have seen how they're bound and how this paper is sealed and -- glued and then sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please move on to the next page. Mr. Dimitrov, could you describe what that is on this page that we see.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: This is the glued piece of paper which you saw from the police, and the seal is from the Republic of Macedonia from the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say that the same text and seal of the Macedonian Ministry of Interior appeared in both books that were in front of you a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I believe that this is the seal from the books, this picture is taken from the books.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps if the witness can be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1321, please. This should be under tabs 6 bis of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, simply for the record, this would be the last page of a much larger document which is 65 ter 1214.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be tab 6 bis, Mr. Dimitrov. Can you see what that is, that is in front of you now on the screen or on the paper copy that you have?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that this is exactly what I was mentioning, the last page of the book which is glued over the book together with the cord.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we'd seek to tender the set of pictures which is Rule 65 ter 1077, as well as the document presently on the screen, which is Rule 65 ter 1D1321 with its translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1077 will become 1D331; 1D1321 will become 1D332.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, I would like to ask you now to turn to tab 2 of your binder, please, and I'll ask the registry to bring up what is Exhibit 1D244, MFI. I don't think we have the right document on the screen. It would be Exhibit 1D244, MFI. Thank you. Mr. Dimitrov, do you recognise the document that is in front of you and could you say what that is, if you do recognise it?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this document. This is a page of the books we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it a part of the book that you gave copy of to the representative of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. This is a page of the book. It says here, page 41, which I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you perhaps describe briefly for the Chamber the process of taking down the names and other details of hotel guests in that book.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Of course. First of all, under item 1 is number, which vary. Each guest receives a particular number. Then the last name and the first name of the foreign guest is registered. The date and place of birth is in column 3. Nationality is listed in column number 4. Type and number of passport, or ID card is in item 5. In item 6, where it is empty, this is for Visas, it is obvious that not many guests needed to have visas to enter Macedonia. Under 7 is the room number of the guest. Number 8, the date of arrival. Number 9, date of departure. And in item 10, are notes, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. And just looking at this page, Mr. Dimitrov, there you can see that under number 241 and 244 the same person appears to have been recorded. And let me ask you this then. In August of 2001, was an entry made every day for every guest? Is that how it was done?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Well, in the period which you're mentioning, the rules which we received, the instructions which we received from the MOI for control of foreign persons, we had to register every day on a daily basis. If a guest were to stay five days, then he would be listed for five days in a row, or 15, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now -- Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to ask my learned colleague not to be so leading when he was asking questions. And secondly, I see that my learned colleague asked about August 2001, and the witness answer in the period you are mentioning, I was wondering whether he is referring basically to August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did the procedure which you indicated, or was the procedure which you've just described a moment ago, was that applicable in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. In August 2001, this procedure was applied. Every person was registered every day individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did that methodology or you said the rules that were imposed by the foreign police department of the MOI, did this methodology changed [sic] at any time, at any point of time?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: When we started working, this was so. However, later on the methodology changed, and now we work under a different methodology, when a guest arrives, one item registers the date of his arrival and the date of departure. Therefore, if he remains with us for five days, he is only in one row, not as previously, when this was listed five times in a row.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as you can recall, or if you can recall, do you remember when these rules applicable to the matter of registration or recording of foreign guests were changed? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: I cannot recall with certainty when this changed, because much time has passed since then. But I do know that since we started working differently than before, that means that the Ministry of Interior told us that we would have to follow a different set of rules and we immediately started applying them as they were indicated to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just looking at the document or the page that you have in front of you, could you say who in your hotel or bed and breakfast is responsible to make those entries into the book?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: At that time which you're bringing up, if you're interested about this period of time, there was a girl by the name of Snjezana Boneva at that time, and she is now Snjezana Vojnovska; she married. She was working there for several years, five or six. I cannot recall precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was there another person or persons that also sometimes made entries into that book?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Since this is a very small bed and breakfast, six room at all, we had two persons employed; Snjezana for the most part did this work. There was another person Dane, I don't recall his last name. So when Snjezana was unable or when she was not working on that shift, it was this person who did this kind of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that information that appears on the guest book, the name of the person, the date and place of birth, nationality and so on, did you record that information in any other document or records that were kept at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: First of all, when the guest comes, we are obliged, because of police registration reasons on a cardboard form to list this information and at the end of the day, in the case that there are guests of course, to take these to the police stations with all of the information which are listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who at the hotel would be responsible to write down or make those -- I think you called them cardboard? Who was that that would do that work?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mainly, as I said before, this was done most frequently by Snjezana Boneva, or Vojnovska now that is her last name at the moment, because she was the person who most often worked in the first shift, in the morning shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who would bring those cartons or cardboards to the police?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: On regular basis, the carton forms were taken to the police by the person who was working on the second afternoon shift and that was most frequently the second receptionist by the name of Dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would such records, that is the name the date of birth and so on and so forth, be made for each and every one of your guests at the hotel both on the guest book and on the cardboards?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: They had to be identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was done or was it done for each and every one of the guests?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. It was always done for every guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you were asked by the representative of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski to review one of the guest books in search of a particular name, the name of a particular person, did you find whether that person had stayed at your hotel in the month of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I determined that this person stayed in the bed and breakfast in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps we can turn to what is page 50 of that document, which would be 1D00-2911, please. That would be page 10 on the paper copy that you've been given, I believe, Mr. Dimitrov. In the Macedonian version, I apologise, this would be 1D00-2895. Mr. Dimitrov, I'll ask you to focus on number 296, the recording number 296. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that the first entry in the guest book which contained the name of that individual for the month of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. That is the first registry in the room 14 of that -- where that individual stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you able to determine whether this person, Mr. Hutsch, had stayed in your hotel at any time prior to the 22nd of August 2001, and I mean earlier in the month of August 2001? Was there any such records made?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Following the guest books, me and Snjezana did not see that the person that you mentioned, Mr. Franz-Josef, was a guest in our hotel in the month of August, apart from this date that we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps if we can go to the next page, please. Is it correct that Mr. Franz-Josef Hutsch is recorded again under number 300 and 305 for the nights of the 23rd to the 24th of August, and from the 24th of August to the 25th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. For each day, just as I mentioned earlier, we had the obligation to register the guest. That is correct. We have the name Franz-Josef Hutsch under the numbers 300 and 305.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And moving on quickly to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we shorten this, Mr. Mettraux. Is it that he is entered in your register each day until the 31st of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It means that he was registered in the guest book until the 31st of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour and perhaps if I could use the last two minutes to seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1D244.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would this be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, those records or guest books that we've looked into, where do you keep them once they've been used and once they're full of entries? Where do you put them?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: The guest books and the entries of each guest, did you mean to ask me where we keep the book itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, we keep the book in our bookkeeping office, once the book is all filled in. The book that is being used is kept at the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And concerning those who are being kept in the bookkeeping office, who has access to that room?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, access to that room is given to the employees, the accountants, the receptionists, in principle, the persons that are employed. Me, including, as well as my supervisors.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something slightly different now. How do you prepare invoices for your guests or customers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, this is not covered by the 92 bis statement is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We understand, Your Honour, and we can explain perhaps what's happened over the course of the weekend. Mr. Dimitrov brought with him the two original books with him together with a couple of invoices which we have given immediately to our colleagues of the Prosecution together with a translation and an indication in the proofing notes that we may ask the witness about this particular matter. The reason we want to ask about it, Your Honour, is because of the matching, if you want, between the invoice and the records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, but be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will be very short, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness -- well, first let me ask you this, a general question, Mr. Dimitrov. Could you tell me who prepares the invoices in your hotel or bed and breakfast.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: The invoices are made usually by the person that works in the first shift. For this particular case the invoices were made by Snjezana Boneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1313, and that would be under tab 3 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, are you able to say who that invoice relates to, what person or guest?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, here we have a receipt, not an invoice. A receipt that was paid in cash. The guest for which this receipt refers to is Hutsch Franz. This is what was typed on the computer, and the receipt that, at the time, could be bought. Again we see the name of the guest Franz-Josef Hutsch, and the amount paid, amount of 28.700 dinars, if that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I will ask you to and the registry, please, to turn to the next page of that document. And would that be the invoice that you just mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: What we are seeing now is one single bill for the stay in August, when Mr. Hutsch slept in the hotel. First, you have the receipt, which is the first document that you showed. That is a receipt for daily exchange, meaning our bookkeeper paid to the bank the amount is 28.700 dinars which means that the bank received this amount of money, the amount that I received from Mr. Hutsch. The second page is the computer report, because we have guest registration in the computer as well. So this is a report about the person Franz Hutsch for the same date, meaning 22nd of August until 31st of August, 2001. And the third page is, again, a bill that we had to have at the time, because the bill has an order number. This is 3155. So this bill we bought and the amount on the bill had to correspond to the amount that is on the receipt and that was paid in the bank, the amount that is paid for that particular person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps -- perhaps very briefly turning to the next page, the third page of that document. Is that the third and last document that you mentioned a moment ago, Mr. Dimitrov?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, yes. That is the third and the last document that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does the information contained in this particular document, in particular the ID number of the person as well as the date of the stay and the room number as well as the name, does it correspond to the information that is recorded in your guest book?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. At the time, on the bill we had to put the information such as the name of the guest, where he came from, and the amount, as well as the number of the nights or days that individual spent in our hotel. So that they can correspond with the receipt and the amount of money that were -- that was deposited in the bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would seek leave to add this particular document to our Rule 65 ter list for the reason we explained. We didn't have the document at the time of filing our list. And I would also seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1D333.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, did you have any reason to believe that anyone falsified the records of your hotel, whether it is the guest book or the invoices that relate to Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: No, I never had any reasons to suspect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one last question, Mr. Dimitrov. For the record, have you ever been convicted of any criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: No. I don't have a record of criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have no further question at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Any questions, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dimitrov. My name is Meritxell Regue and I'm appearing on behalf of the Prosecution and I will be asking you some questions today. Mr. Dimitrov, the hotel Dal Met Fu is part of the Dal Fufo Corporation, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: It is correct that the hotel Dal Met Fu is part of Dal Fufo. I have to also mention this, that each unit works individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. And the other shareholder and co-owner of this corporation is Ljupco Nikolovski, your first cousin, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, Ljupco Nikolovski is my second cousin.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me. But is he still the co-owner or the shareholder of this corporation of the hotel Dal Met Fu?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: The documents which we have state that his sister is the co-owner, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. And your company, your corporation, not only owns the hotel but it also owns several restaurants in Skopje and Macedonia, catering service companies and also some restaurants in Greece, right? And I would ask for a brief answer, Mr. Dimitrov, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You must be a busy person, right, with a hectic schedule, travelling quite often due to work commitments, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue, I travel quite often. About being busy, of course, I am very busy. My work hours extend 12 hours or more.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the hotel Dal Met Fu, despite being small, has become quite an upscale bed and breakfast where an important number of foreigners stay over the year, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, if you wish to say that there distinguished or that my establishment has become upscale, that I would agree with you and I would thank you for your compliments.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And would you also agree that as customers, as clients you have an important number of foreigners?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I agree with you that I have a large number of foreign customers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And would you agree also that the hotel has several restaurants, Restaurant Galija, for example, or Dal Met Fu, Dal Fufo restaurant, and these restaurants are frequented by prominent people of the Macedonian society, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And just to clarify the hotel is located in Macedonia Square which is downtown Skopje, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And well, as a prominent businessman you must be aware and also as a lawyer, you must be aware, actually of the applicable law to your type of business, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue. I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And also the importance of respecting the law, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: I agree with you, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dimitrov, just to clarify, when your hotel start operating, start running as a bed and breakfast?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I remember the date 23rd of May, 2001. I remember this day precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. And when, in your statement you say that you were the director of the hotel since 1993, before, I think, sorry, what did you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I wanted to say that the restaurant existed since 1991 and I am director of the restaurant. The hotel, or, rather, the bed and breakfast is only a part of the restaurant. All of this is part of the same company of which I am the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks for the clarification. Mr. Dimitrov, you may recall a visit of an investigator of this Tribunal together with his interpreter in October 2001. He came to your hotel requesting copies of the lists of guests from July and August 2000, 2001, and 2002. Do you recall his visit, Mr. Dimitrov, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, Mr. Thomas, again, my apologies, I cannot recall his last name, I have met twice with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You met twice with him. And in one of these encounters, an employee of yours, a Snjezana Boneva, I believe, made some copies for Mr. Thomas Kuehnel of two guest books, foreign guest books of the hotel. The first foreign guest book which runs from May 2001 until March 2002, and the second foreign guest book which runs from March 2002 till March 2004. Do you recall that, Mr. Dimitrov?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, yes, I do recall this, because I received Mr. Kuehnel, and I took him to see Mrs. Vojnovska. This is again the same person, Ms. Boneva at the time. Therefore, I took him to see Mrs. Vojnovska and I told him that she would assist with him anything he might need.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please go to 65 ter 1217 which is tab 13 of Your Honour's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And it should be --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I will first distribute the binders, my apologies. No, we're going to give you a binder, Mr. Dimitrov. In e-court it should be the page 15 in Macedonian, and there is only one English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could focus in paragraph 2. This is Article -- it is tab 13 of your binder, Mr. Dimitrov. You are going to be looking at Article 73 of the Law on Residence of Movement of Foreigners, dated 1992, which was applicable in 2001. Article 73.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see it, Mr. Dimitrov? If we read the second paragraph -- well, the first paragraph starts: "As enterprises and other legal entities and individuals who provide services on a paid accommodation for foreigners, are obliged to keep record of the foreigners, book on foreigners." And then the second paragraph reads and I quote: "The records of foreigners shall be kept in a period of two years from the day it was concluded." Mr. Dimitrov, would you agree with me that the law states that the foreign guest books should be kept for a period of two years, meaning if you finish your first guest book in March 2002, legally have you to keep until March 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: The book of foreigners which you mentioned, yes. But I was referring to the bills, and the need to keep them for seven years.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. But would you agree with me that the law only requires that the book of foreigners should be kept for two years. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue. Here it says that the records for foreigners should be kept for a period of two years from the date it was concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to 1D330, which is tab 1, is the 92 bis statement of yourself, Mr. Dimitrov. If we could go to the next page, please. Mr. Dimitrov, you will see that in paragraph 2 of your statement you mention that proper records are kept of all the hotel guests in the register of guests. In keeping with the regulations, the register of guests must be kept for seven years. Yet, Mr. Dimitrov, we have seen what the law says, but in your statement you were quite clear that the books had to be kept for seven years. Mr. Dimitrov, either -- would you agree with me, Mr. Dimitrov, that you actually were incorrect in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I previously said when we were discussing my statement that I wasn't sure whether I had read this someplace or whether some from my accounting office told me this.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, here paragraph 2 is quite clear, Mr. Dimitrov. It says: "Must be kept." And when you met with the representative of the registry of this Tribunal in January 2008, I believe that you were given the opportunity, right, to modify or to correct your statement and you didn't do so, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, when I said for the first time to speak about my statement, I said clearly and it is probably included in the transcript, I mentioned that I wasn't certain how long this book should be kept, whether I had heard this somewhere or whether I had read it somewhere. Whether I read this or whether my accountant told me this. This was told to the representative from the registry of the ICTY to confirm my statement. It was a lady with dark hair. I apologise, I don't remember the name. I did this in front of her, the attorney Godzo and Kumovski [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Dimitrov, apparently this is not recorded in your 92 bis statement so I believe you that did not say that because it's not recorded. But now I will move on. If we could please go to 65 ter -- well, before that, Mr. Dimitrov you have testified that you have not been convicted with criminal charges, but have you ever been indicted with criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Previously, I had mentioned that I have not been convicted of a criminal act; indicted, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please go to 65 ter 1211. It is tab 2 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go we would like to have ask for specification on the part of the Prosecution about the alleged relevance of that document. We have sent an email to the Office of the Prosecution over the course of the weekend to query this matter and try to determine with them what the alleged relevance of that document is and the Prosecution has declined to give that indication to the Defence. And we would be grateful if the Prosecution would be able at this stage to give an indication to that effect which would allow us, if necessary, to object to the presentation of this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that this document goes to the credibility and to the honesty of this witness and the witness's evidence that he has given today in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it your case that he was convicted on this indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as we know, we know that this is a pending indictment issued in 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Pending, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, we believe the proceeding is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise for taking the Court's time, Your Honour. I simply wish to indicate that this matter has already been litigated at least on one occasion with the witness Mr. Kuehnel where a similar issue arose. At page 7973 to 7977, it was clearly indicated that an indictment was proof of no matter relevant to the credit. Furthermore, as indicated by my colleague, those proceedings are pending. Furthermore, as we understand it and to the extent that we can assist, the trial in this case has not even started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can I present the evidence now, Your Honours. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could please go to tab 2, Mr. Dimitrov. I will try to be quite brief. We can see in the first page that the basic public prosecutor is issuing an indictment against Ljupco Nikolovski, owner of the corporation Dal Met Fu and yourself, Branislav Dimitrov. I just notice that in the third line, number 2, it says, that have you secondary school education. Mr. Dimitrov, which is correct, secondary school education or did you study law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: May I respond by saying that two mistakes have been made. The first one regarding the fact that it states that I have finished secondary school education. If it is necessary, through DHL or by other means I can send to you my original diploma. The second mistake is in regards that Ljupco Nikolovski, the owner of the corporation Dal Met Fu. In the documents this is not listed anywhere, so this is the second mistake that is made. The ownership papers do not have his name anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Dimitrov, that will be litigated in Court. I forgot to mention that the date of this indictment is the 2nd of May, 2007. If you see in the paragraph below, basically it says, Mr. Dimitrov, that you and your partner fail to pay some debts back in 2001, which were actually judicially declared and then you apply for bankruptcy procedure in February 2003. If we could please go to the second page. In the second page, we see that in the first paragraph it reads that due to these actions, you and your partner allegedly committed the criminal act of false bankruptcy which is described in Article 254 in relation to Article 22 of the Macedonian Criminal Code. And then we see that the prosecutor proposes several measures, but I will skip that. If we could go please, to the third page, briefly. We see that in Roman number III, the prosecutor requests to the Court, to declare the accused, meaning yourself and your cousin, culpable. And if we move to the paragraph, starting during February 2003, basically the paragraph repeats that in 2003, you and your partner initiated a bankruptcy procedure to avoid paying some debts. The last paragraph reads and I quote: "The above stated facts emerge beyond doubt from the written evidence supplemented by verbal statements of all witnesses." Mr. Dimitrov, in the course of these proceedings you did issue a statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Should I start responding, Ms. Regue? First of all --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Please, if you could -- my apologies. If could you just answer my question whether in the course of these proceedings you did issue a statement before the investigative judge or the prosecutor. That was my only question, Mr. Dimitrov.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, on the 11th of March, as scheduled as a date for the trial, not the 2nd of May; and secondly, it is true that I gave a statement in front of investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. If we could move, please, to page 4. The second paragraph starting on 6th of June, 2002, explains that the bankruptcy procedure was -- well, explains the bankruptcy procedure and how it was closed because the debtor, meaning yourself, was not found in possession of any property, after a review of statements on the economic and financial situation of the debtor, and upon a statement of the representative of the debtor. But, Mr. Dimitrov, you have testified that you have been the -- you are actually and you have been the owner of the hotel Dal Met Fu at least since 2001, and the restaurant, I believe, since 1993, right, so you did have some properties at that time?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Do you want me to respond to you, Ms. Regue? There is a mistake again and the mistake is what I told you in the beginning, that each unit works independently. That's one. Number two, the bankruptcy procedure was for the restaurant which is --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, my only question was about your ownership. Here you are not being tried about this proceeding. My only question was whether back in 2001 or even before that, you or yourself through any of your companies were actually owning restaurants or hotels, as I understood that you testified that here before this Court.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, this is where your mistake is. The company was litigated, not me personally. There was a debt of 800 dinars that the company was supposed to pay, not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. I will move on. In the second paragraph, indeed it is mentioned -- excuse me, can we move to page 5 and I will just finish. The second paragraph of page 5 of this document states that you indeed issue some allegations and you said that your bank account had been blocked and actually the prosecutor finds these allegation -- these allegations untruthful. And, finally the prosecutor states that you and your partner's conduct falls within the category of the criminal act of false bankruptcy. Mr. Dimitrov, you were indeed dishonest before an investigating judge, right, to avoid fulfilling with your legal obligations, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I am very sorry that I have to reiterate that you make a mistake again. It is the company that is litigated, not the person. Maybe this is a difference between the legal system in your country and in my country, but the company was litigated, not me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Waiting for you to be sure that the witness had finished. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the proposition that my colleague has just made was a rather serious one and we won't object to any serious propositions being made to the witness to the extent that it would allow to test the credibility of the witness but we believe that it has to be made fairly and that before accusing the witness of having been dishonest with her, in a judicial proceeding or otherwise, a basis for such assertion should be established, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was basically quoting what the prosecutor said with regards to the allegations. But I will move on from this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As the Chamber sees it at the moment, Ms. Regue, there is an allegation in an indictment which has not been tried.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, the witness says this was a corporate debt, not his personal debt.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's what I understood from his evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, what else do you see that could be relevant to this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was going to put to this witness, Your Honours, that in the course of the proceedings it seems that the legal or the financial representative of this witness presented some documentation to the -- to a court of justice in order to declare false bankruptcy. In other words, that false documentation was presented before a court of law. And that's -- that's what is being tried right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, this Chamber has problems with you in fact if that's where you're intending to go, asking this witness whether in this proceeding which is pending against him in another court, he has been guilty of what you would clearly allege to be criminal conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I simply meant that he was dishonest. My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before -- dishonest to a court is what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Investigative judge, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It's not an issue that we can try. It's away from the facts of this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, I will move on from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would be far better because we would, I fear, have to stop you at any moment now because of the nature of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was done, Your Honour, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Dimitrov, you have testified -- you have testified about the way of recording the entry of the guests in the foreign guest book, right, and you have testified how at some point in time, the recording of the guests changed, but you are not aware of the time when that happened actually. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, I cannot determine the exact date when the change occurred. It was noticed in the control of foreign data before the Ministry of Interior Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Dimitrov, that the first book which you gave to the investigator Thomas Kuehnel has one way of recording and the second book which starts in March 2002, already works with the second way of recording the entry of the guests?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, if you say so, then I believe it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For example, if we could go briefly to tab 3, which is Exhibit 1D244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to interrupt once again but just as a matter of clarification upon the question of my colleague is the suggestion being made that the new methodology was implemented immediately on to the second book. We believe if that's the suggestion that is made, that is quite incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was the suggestion that I was making by my learned colleague maybe can deal with that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Dimitrov, do you see that in the entry -- well, basically in this first guest book, Mr. Dimitrov, you already testified that if one guest stays several days, there will be a single entry for every single day that this person stays at your hotel, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue. When we started to work that is the principle that we used, the one that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For example, in the entry 245, we see actually one person who stayed in the hotel from the 9th to the 10th of August, 2001, right? And if we could go to the second page, please, of this exhibit. And if you could, please, look at the entry 247, we can see the same person who stayed there the following night, basically, from the 10th to the 11th of August, 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, yes. And the same person appears under the number 251.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. If now we could go, please, to 65 ter 1213, which is tab 10, and it should be the page 36 in e-court. And there is no English translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it should be ERN -- the page with ERN N006-5801, and it bears the number 35 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you find, Mr. Dimitrov? It's tab 10. It should be the page with number 35 in the upper right corner of your document. If you wish, can you look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes. I see what you're showing to me. But there is probably a mistake here. On the document that I have, it says it is page 42 and what you are showing on the screen is page 35. If you are talking about the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Look, Mr. Dimitrov, we move to another document. If you could please go to tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid time is going to prevent you, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I just have one minute, Your Honour. I just have one minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Half one minute, I believe you. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If could you please go to tab 10. We should see number 35 on the upper right side. Mr. Dimitrov, this is the second guest book, the one which goes from March 2002 to March 2004. And if we could see it in the screen, please. Just -- sorry, if we could go, please, to page 36 in e-court, which would be page 35 in the hard copy. The next page in e-court, please. Thanks. Mr. Dimitrov, just briefly, do you see that in the second guest book the entry with the number 208, a person from Tripoli or born in Tripoli, he check in in your hotel the 22nd, I believe, of April 2002, at 2.00 a.m., and he check out on the 1st of May, 2002. Do you see that in this second guest book there is only one single entry for the stay of one person in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV DIMITROV
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Dimitrov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but once again the question was formulated in such a way by my colleague to suggest that this would be the case in all parts of the book. I think if she were to ask about this particular page of the book, it would be an appropriate question. We do believe, however, that it could mislead the witness to suggest it is the same manner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Mettraux, you better not go on to what the witness may or may not say about it. That will be perhaps a matter for cross-examination tomorrow. We must adjourn now to continue tomorrow at 2.15. I am afraid, Mr. Dimitrov, we must ask you to return tomorrow when the questioning will continue. We will commence sitting at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really feel very comfortable here. So I don't mind at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We won't arrange to extend your stay longer than necessary. We will adjourn. I'm a little worried how long this will take because Mr. Apostolski was hoping to open tomorrow, and I --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Being conservative, I would say 40 minutes. Being conservative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 40 minutes. We will not be able to sit the full length of time tomorrow and will need to adjourn by between quarter to 6.00 and 6.00, and we certainly want to give Mr. Apostolski his full time for opening, so if counsel can keep that in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of March, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
